text: {"contradictions":[{"source":"فَحَلَقْتُ وَأَفَقْتُ","english":"I shaved my head and woke up","kind":"sense","why":"The verb 'halaqtu' here refers to the act of shaving the head as a sign of repentance or distress, not literally shaving one's head.","certainty":"medium"}],"omissions":[{"source":"وَتُخْلِقَ يُخْلِقُ مِنْ أَبْتَلَى فَصَبَرَ"}],"additions":[{"english":"The commentator emphasizes that the loss of money is a small price to pay for the wisdom gained through the encounter with the trickster Abu Zayd."}]}

contradictions.english: I shaved my head and woke up
contradictions.why: The verb 'halaqtu' here refers to the act of shaving the head as a sign of repentance or distress, not literally shaving one's head.

additions.english: The commentator emphasizes that the loss of money is a small price to pay for the wisdom gained through the encounter with the trickster Abu Zayd.
